interest: This document provides valuable insight into U.S. inter-departmental intelligence tracking during the interwar period, specifically how the Department of State and the U.S. Navy monitored Japanese covert operations within third-party nations. It highlights early Japanese efforts to recruit foreign nationals—specifically British subjects such as W. H. Greene—to conduct espionage against American military and territorial interests in the continental United States and the Philippines. Additionally, it illustrates State Department archival practices, demonstrating how cross-reference docket sheets were maintained for specific decimal subjects even when the underlying investigative reports were routed into broader espionage or biographical files.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.20241) consists of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet recording documents related to Japanese military activities, intelligence gathering, and espionage in Great Britain during 1934. The sheet indexes two separate reports: a February 1934 report (No. 61) from the U.S. Naval Attaché in Great Britain concerning the recruitment and employment of British subjects by Japanese intelligence for espionage operations directed against the United States and the Philippines, and an April 1934 communication from Admiral William H. Standley of the Navy Department forwarding a London Naval Attaché report regarding W. H. Greene, a British subject suspected of conducting espionage on behalf of Japan. Both substantive reports were cross-referenced and filed under other decimal classifications (894.20211/118 and 811.111-Greene, W.H.), leaving this docket sheet as the record for Japanese espionage activities in the United Kingdom.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers indexing records on Japanese military activities and espionage in Great Britain.
subfiles.summary: This 'List of Papers' docket sheet indexes two U.S. naval intelligence reports from early 1934 concerning Japanese espionage activities in Great Britain. The first entry records a February 2, 1934 report (No. 61) from the U.S. Naval Attaché in Great Britain regarding the employment of British subjects by Japan for espionage purposes in the United States or the Philippines. The second entry records an April 11, 1934 transmission from Admiral William H. Standley of the Navy Department forwarding a report from the Naval Attaché at London concerning W. H. Greene, a British subject engaged in espionage on behalf of Japan. Both entries note that the underlying documents were cross-referenced and transferred to other files (894.20211/118 and 811.111-Greene, W.H.).
subfiles.title: List of Papers: Military Activities of Japan in Great Britain
